paragraphs: Point cloud registration aligns two collections of 3D points describing a scene. CAST addresses this task without requiring prior knowledge of their relative pose. The paper targets a weakness in coarse-to-fine matching: early correspondences can be sparse and geometrically inconsistent, leaving later stages with substantial work to recover a coherent alignment.

CAST introduces two attention mechanisms that address this problem during feature matching. Spot-guided cross-attention focuses comparisons on relevant regions across the point clouds, reducing interference from unrelated areas. Consistency-aware self-attention strengthens correspondences that agree geometrically. Together, these components make geometric agreement part of the matching process before the final alignment is estimated.

A lightweight fine-matching module then estimates the transformation using either sparse keypoints or dense features. Experiments on outdoor LiDAR and indoor RGBD datasets report state-of-the-art accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. These findings support the approach across both sensing settings and connect its early consistency checks to the practical need for efficient registration in applications such as robotic odometry.
neurips-2024-a-consistency-aware-spot-gu.tldr: CAST improves point cloud alignment by directing attention toward relevant regions and geometrically consistent matches.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to align two point clouds when neither the correspondence between points nor their relative orientation is known. Its planted model assumes that one dataset is a noisy version of the other, with an orthogonal transformation and a relabeling applied. Alignment quality is measured through Euclidean transport cost between the clouds.

The theoretical analysis examines what information permits in two regimes: dimension much larger than the logarithm of the number of points, and dimension much smaller than that quantity. This separates questions about the information available in the observations from questions about how an algorithm can use it. The setting also connects to aligning graphs generated from geometric data.

For computation, the authors introduce Ping-Pong, which alternates between estimating the transformation and estimating point correspondences, starting from a convex relaxation. They give sufficient conditions for recovering the planted signal after one step; this is a conditional result. Experiments compare the method with an existing approach, without the abstract specifying the comparison's outcome.
neurips-2024-aligning-embeddings-and-geo.tldr: The paper analyzes when noisy point clouds can be aligned and proposes an alternating algorithm with conditional one-step recovery guarantees.

paragraphs: This paper establishes a mathematical property for single-parameter natural exponential families, a class of probability distributions. Under a subexponential tail assumption, it proves self-concordance with polynomial-sized parameters. Self-concordance controls how curvature changes, and here it becomes a tool for analyzing learning algorithms whose observations follow these distributions.

For the more restrictive subgaussian case, the authors give an exact characterization of how the self-concordance parameter grows. The distinction matters because the results specify how properties of the reward distribution affect the mathematical quantities used in the analysis. The guarantees depend on these stated distributional assumptions rather than applying to arbitrary reward distributions.

The application concerns generalized linear bandits, where an algorithm repeatedly chooses actions and learns from rewards. The resulting regret bounds for optimistic algorithms scale with the optimal arm's reward variance and avoid exponential dependence on the problem-parameter bound in the leading term. The authors also establish a bound for subexponential rewards, extending the covered settings to Poisson, exponential, and gamma bandits.
neurips-2024-almost-free-self-concordanc.tldr: New self-concordance results yield variance-sensitive regret bounds for generalized linear bandits, including several subexponential reward families.

paragraphs: Parametric partial differential equations describe systems whose behavior changes with parameters and conditions. This creates a challenge for neural solvers: trajectories learned under one configuration may not capture the dynamics of another. The paper studies conditioning mechanisms that let a solver account for these variations, finding adaptive conditioning particularly effective for generalization.

Existing adaptive methods can become difficult to scale as the number of parameters requiring adjustment increases. GEPS addresses this with first-order optimization and a low-rank adaptation mechanism operating on a small set of context parameters. The approach makes rapid adaptation central to handling changing conditions while reducing the scope of what must be adjusted.

The authors demonstrate GEPS with both fully data-driven solvers and solvers that incorporate physical knowledge. Across spatiotemporal forecasting problems, they report strong generalization to unseen initial conditions, equation coefficients, forcing terms, and solution domains. These findings indicate that the adaptation mechanism can support several distinct kinds of variation, with its reported effectiveness spanning both types of neural solver.
neurips-2024-boosting-generalization-in-.tldr: GEPS improves neural PDE solvers' generalization through rapid, low-rank adaptation of a small set of context parameters.

paragraphs: A classifier often assigns a score to every possible label and returns whichever has the largest score. Even small score changes can switch that choice when competing labels are close. The paper identifies this discontinuous final decision as a source of instability under slight changes to the training data.

The proposed pipeline addresses both score construction and label selection. It uses bagging, which combines predictions obtained through resampling and averaging, to produce stable continuous scores. It then replaces ordinary argmax with an inflated argmax that returns a set of candidate labels. Allowing a set makes the final output less sensitive to small changes that would otherwise flip a single winning label.

The resulting stability guarantee requires no distributional assumptions, applies to any base classifier, and does not depend on the number of classes or input dimensions. On a benchmark dataset, the authors demonstrate protection against instability without losing accuracy. That empirical accuracy finding accompanies a broader theoretical stability result; the output's set-valued form is central to the construction.
neurips-2024-building-a-stable-classifie.tldr: Bagging and a set-valued inflated argmax produce classifiers with distribution-free stability guarantees.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning learns a policy from a fixed dataset without additional feedback from the environment. A learned dynamics model can guide policy search, but limited data can leave it inaccurate for unfamiliar states and actions. Policies may then exploit overestimated values in regions that the dataset does not adequately support.

C-LAP addresses this through a generative model of observations and actions together. Policy learning is constrained to remain within the support of the model's latent action distribution. The generative model then places an implicit constraint on the actions it produces. This moves the protective mechanism into action generation, eliminating the method's need for additional uncertainty penalties in Bellman updates.

The authors report that this design substantially reduces the gradient steps needed to learn a policy. Evaluations on D4RL and V-D4RL find performance competitive with state-of-the-art approaches, with particularly strong results on visual-observation datasets. The findings support latent action constraints as a useful approach to policy learning when both dynamics and action choices must be learned from fixed data.
neurips-2024-constrained-latent-action-p.tldr: C-LAP constrains policies through a learned latent action distribution, reducing training steps and performing especially well with visual observations.

paragraphs: Model-based offline reinforcement learning often penalizes uncertain rewards to discourage decisions outside the training data's coverage. Policy evaluation commonly estimates Bellman targets using Monte Carlo samples. The paper identifies randomness in this estimation step as a significant cause of slow convergence and theoretically relates suboptimality to the number of samples used per target.

MOMBO replaces that sampling step with a deterministic approximation based on progressive moment matching. It carries uncertainty about the next state through a nonlinear Q-network, approximating each hidden layer's activation distribution with a normal distribution. This allows the target calculation to account for uncertainty without repeatedly estimating it through random draws.

The contribution therefore concerns how uncertain future values are computed within policy evaluation. The authors show that tighter suboptimality guarantees are possible for MOMBO than for existing Monte Carlo approaches. They also observe faster convergence across a large set of benchmark tasks. These results combine a theoretical benefit with empirical evidence, while retaining the stated normal-distribution approximation inside the network.
neurips-2024-deterministic-uncertainty-p.tldr: MOMBO deterministically propagates uncertainty through a Q-network, enabling tighter suboptimality guarantees and faster observed convergence.

paragraphs: Federated learning faces a tension between keeping local model updates private and identifying malicious updates. Secure aggregation hides the information that many anomaly detectors need to inspect. Some existing approaches combine the two protections by introducing extra parties or assuming that two servers do not collude, complicating their deployment.

DDFed combines encrypted aggregation with anomaly detection while preserving the existing federated learning topology and participant roles. It uses fully homomorphic encryption to support computation on encrypted updates. Its two-phase detection procedure combines secure similarity computation with collaborative selection driven by feedback. Additional measures address potential privacy breaches caused by Byzantine clients during detection.

The authors evaluate DDFed against various model poisoning attacks in both cross-device and cross-silo scenarios. Experiments on public datasets report protection of model privacy alongside effective resistance to the tested poisoning threats. The significance is that privacy and robustness are handled within one framework, with encrypted-update analysis providing a way to address the visibility problem created by secure aggregation.
neurips-2024-dual-defense-enhancing-priv.tldr: DDFed combines encrypted aggregation and collaborative anomaly detection to protect privacy and mitigate federated learning poisoning attacks.

paragraphs: The paper examines interference from neural-network channels that are irrelevant to the current input's category. Its motivation is that useful information can be concentrated in a sparse subset of channels, while existing activation mechanisms may leave distracting responses active. Those responses can affect the network's final decision even when they carry irrelevant or redundant information.

Dual-Perspective Activation, or DPA, identifies and suppresses these channels using a criterion constructed during training from both forward and backward propagation. It preserves responses in relevant channels while removing channel noise. The mechanism is trainable as part of the full network and introduces no additional parameters, making the denoising operation compatible with end-to-end learning.

Experiments report successful channel denoising, sparser representations, and strong performance relative to other activation mechanisms across multiple tasks and domains. The authors also describe DPA as fast and applicable to many mainstream architectures. These findings support using information from both propagation directions to decide which activations should contribute to a network's prediction.
neurips-2024-dual-perspective-activation.tldr: DPA uses forward and backward propagation signals to suppress irrelevant channels without adding parameters.

paragraphs: Text-to-video systems can produce visually appealing scenes while giving little movement to actions described in the prompt. The paper attributes this problem to text representations that overlook motion and conditioning mechanisms that inadequately communicate temporal information. DEMO addresses both parts of that pathway, from understanding the description to guiding video generation.

The framework separates content from motion in its text encoding. A content encoder represents static elements, while a motion encoder represents temporal dynamics. Separate conditioning mechanisms pass these two kinds of information into generation. Text-motion and video-motion supervision further strengthen the model's ability to understand motion descriptions and produce corresponding movement.

Evaluations on MSR-VTT, UCF-101, WebVid-10M, EvalCrafter, and VBench report improved motion dynamics while maintaining high visual quality. The findings support explicitly representing motion at multiple stages of the system. By giving temporal information its own encoding and conditioning path, DEMO makes the actions in a prompt a more direct part of the generation process.
neurips-2024-enhancing-motion-in-text-to.tldr: DEMO separates content and motion in text encoding and conditioning to generate more dynamic videos while preserving visual quality.

paragraphs: A preference between two language-model responses can depend on unstated criteria or the person making the judgment. This makes direct preference feedback hard to interpret and potentially inconsistent. The paper treats preference modeling as two decisions: selecting the relevant context and evaluating the responses according to that context.

The authors decompose reward-modeling error along these two stages. Their analysis suggests that supervising context alongside context-specific preferences may help models accommodate diverse human preferences. To test the second stage, they construct preference-reversal datasets that separate context-specific choices from general preferences. This design makes it harder for a model to succeed simply by repeating its usual preference regardless of the stated context.

Experiments show that existing preference models benefit from context but do not fully use it. The authors also fine-tune a context-aware reward model whose context-specific performance exceeds GPT-4 and Llama 3 70B in their evaluation. The results establish a targeted capability improvement and motivate further investigation of context-aware preference modeling's value for alignment.
neurips-2024-improving-context-aware-pre.tldr: Preference-reversal datasets reveal incomplete context use in reward models and support training models to evaluate context-specific preferences.

paragraphs: Dynamic graph models must handle relationships that change over time, including shifts in the environments generating the data. The paper separates this challenge into inferring environmental factors and using those factors effectively. EpoD combines prompt learning with a structural causal model to address both parts within one dynamic graph learning approach.

A self-prompted learning mechanism first infers unseen environmental factors. The model then introduces a causal pathway in which dynamic subgraphs act as mediators. These subgraphs incorporate the inferred environment variables into dependencies between nodes, allowing the graph representation to capture changes in the data distribution. Environmental information therefore influences the relationships the model uses for prediction.

The authors provide theoretical discussion and intuitive analysis supporting generalization and interpretability. Experiments across seven real-world datasets from different domains report performance superior to the evaluated baselines. Toy examples further support the interpretation of the model's behavior. Together, these results support connecting environment inference to a structured mechanism for changing how a dynamic graph represents node dependencies.
neurips-2024-improving-generalization-of.tldr: EpoD infers environmental factors and incorporates them through dynamic subgraphs to improve generalization under changing graph conditions.

paragraphs: This paper introduces a dataset connecting indoor air-quality measurements with occupants' daily activities in low- to middle-income communities in India. It addresses limited study of indoor pollution in these settings. Measurements come from 30 indoor sites across four regions encompassing rural, suburban, and urban locations, collected over six months covering summer and winter.

The sites include homes, studio apartments, classrooms, research laboratories, and food canteens. Occupants provide real-time activity labels through a speech-to-text application, adding information about what was happening alongside the pollution readings. This pairing provides a basis for investigating how pollutant patterns vary with activities and indoor environments.

The dataset also contains missing measurements caused by power failures and network outages, creating a concrete need for cleaning and imputation methods. The authors identify potential uses including finding recurring pollution sources, forecasting exposure, informing room design, and building pollution-aware recommendation systems. These are proposed research opportunities enabled by the dataset, whose central contribution is measurement coverage combined with activity annotations.
neurips-2024-indoor-air-quality-dataset-.tldr: A dataset pairs six months of indoor air-quality measurements from 30 Indian sites with occupant-reported daily activities.

paragraphs: Event cameras capture local edge and motion information, making reconstruction of conventional video inherently ambiguous. This ambiguity can produce artifacts and blurred regions. LaSe-E2V adds language guidance to supply semantic information, using text-conditioned diffusion models to help reconstruct videos with a more coherent understanding of scene content.

Diffusion models also introduce diversity and randomness that complicate spatial and temporal consistency. The framework addresses this with event-guided spatiotemporal attention that feeds event information into denoising. An event-aware mask loss promotes coherence over time, while a noise initialization strategy improves spatial consistency. These components connect the semantic guidance from text with the structure supplied by the event stream.

Because paired event, text, and video data were unavailable, the authors combine existing reconstruction datasets and generate descriptions using tagging models. Experiments on three datasets, including fast-motion and low-light scenarios, report superior reconstruction performance. The findings support language as a useful source of semantic guidance when combined with mechanisms specifically designed to preserve consistency in event-based reconstruction.
neurips-2024-lase-e2v-towards-language-g.tldr: LaSe-E2V combines language-guided diffusion with event-specific consistency mechanisms to improve video reconstruction from event cameras.

paragraphs: The paper studies how an agent can learn a reusable representation from offline data collected across several reinforcement learning tasks. Its central assumption is that these tasks share a common representation. The learner's goal is to recover that shared structure from existing datasets so it can support learning on a subsequent task.

The authors analyze this question in the setting of low-rank reinforcement learning and introduce MORL, an algorithm for offline multitask representation learning. The upstream stage focuses on learning the representation across tasks. The downstream stage introduces a new task that shares the same representation, making this common structure the basis for transfer.

The theoretical investigation covers downstream reward-free, offline, and online scenarios. Its results demonstrate benefits from reusing the upstream representation compared with directly learning the low-rank model's representation for the new task. This establishes a theoretical reason to combine offline experience across related tasks. The shared-representation assumption is essential to the setting in which the transfer benefits are studied.
neurips-2024-offline-multitask-represent.tldr: MORL learns a shared representation from offline tasks, with theoretical benefits for new tasks that share that representation.

paragraphs: Image restoration fairness concerns whether an algorithm treats different image groups equally well. The paper argues that existing definitions can be too rigid because they classify a reconstruction as entirely incorrect whenever it falls outside its group's ground-truth image set. That binary treatment can obscure the different ways restoration errors appear.

The authors introduce the Group Perceptual Index, or GPI, which measures statistical distance between a group's ground-truth image distribution and its reconstruction distribution. Fairness is assessed by comparing these distances across groups. Under their definition, perfect perceptual fairness means that every group has the same GPI, making equal distributional discrepancy the criterion.

This changes the assessment from a binary judgment about individual group membership to a comparison of reconstruction distributions. The authors motivate the definition, analyze it theoretically, and relate it to earlier fairness notions. They also demonstrate its usefulness with state-of-the-art face restoration algorithms. The contribution is an alternative framework for evaluating fairness that can reflect differences in perceptual error across groups.
neurips-2024-perceptual-fairness-in-imag.tldr: The paper defines perceptual fairness by comparing distributional differences between original and restored images across groups.

paragraphs: Performative control studies systems whose underlying dynamics change in response to the controller's chosen policy. This means both the observed state distribution and its temporal correlations depend on that policy. The paper introduces a performatively stable control solution and examines when such a solution exists and can be reached.

The authors first provide a sufficient condition for a unique solution, accounting for how distributional sensitivities propagate and aggregate over time. For almost surely strongly stable dynamics, a solution exists when the summed sensitivities are sufficiently small. For almost surely unstable dynamics, existence requires sensitivities to decay in a temporally backward direction. The two statements have different logical strengths: one supplies an existence condition, while the other identifies a necessity.

The paper then presents a repeated stochastic gradient descent scheme that converges to the stable solution and analyzes its finite-time convergence rate. Numerical results support the theory. Together, the contributions connect the system's stability and sensitivity to policy changes with the feasibility of finding a stable controller.
neurips-2024-performative-control-for-li.tldr: The paper establishes conditions for stable control when policies alter system dynamics and gives a convergent gradient-based scheme.

paragraphs: Predicting molecular properties with only a few labeled molecules makes adaptation difficult, even when a molecular encoder has already been pretrained. The paper attributes ineffective fine-tuning to too many adjustable parameters relative to the available labels and to encoders that do not adequately use task context. Pin-Tuning addresses both issues.

The method adds lightweight adapters to pretrained message-passing layers and uses Bayesian weight consolidation for atom and bond embedding layers. These components support parameter-efficient adaptation while guarding against overfitting and forgetting pretrained knowledge. The adapters are also made context-aware, allowing the encoder's adaptation to reflect information relevant to the particular few-shot prediction task.

This extends contextual adaptation into the molecular encoder itself, alongside the context-aware classification already used in this setting. Evaluations on public datasets report better tuning and improved few-shot prediction with fewer trainable parameters. The results support combining a restricted adaptation mechanism with task context when labeled molecular examples are scarce and preserving pretrained information is valuable.
neurips-2024-pin-tuning-parameter-effici.tldr: Pin-Tuning combines context-aware adapters and weight consolidation to improve few-shot molecular prediction with fewer trainable parameters.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization links an outer optimization problem to an inner one, making its gradient calculations more involved than those of a single-level problem. The paper focuses on how training examples are selected during stochastic optimization. It argues that the usual assumption of independent sampling can increase computational costs because of the special structure of the hypergradient.

The authors introduce an algorithm based on sampling without replacement and prove a faster convergence rate than counterparts using independent sampling. This makes example selection a central algorithmic design choice. The theoretical improvement concerns how rapidly the optimization procedure converges, connecting the sampling strategy to the cost of solving the nested problem.

The analysis extends beyond standard bilevel optimization to conditional bilevel problems and to minimax and compositional optimization as special cases. Experiments on synthetic problems and real-world applications report advantages for the proposed algorithms. Taken together, the theoretical and numerical findings show that revisiting sampling assumptions can improve methods across several related optimization settings.
neurips-2024-provably-faster-algorithms-.tldr: Without-replacement sampling yields provably faster convergence for bilevel optimization algorithms, with supporting numerical results.

paragraphs: This paper studies the optimal memory capacity of modern Hopfield models and kernelized Hopfield models, a transformer-compatible form of dense associative memory. It connects stored memory configurations to spherical codes from information theory. Through this connection, memorization becomes a geometric problem about arranging points on a high-dimensional sphere.

The analysis shows that kernelized Hopfield models reach optimal capacity when their feature space permits memories to form an optimal spherical code. The authors identify necessary conditions and establish an upper capacity bound matching the known exponential lower bound asymptotically. Matching the bounds gives a tight characterization of capacity at that asymptotic scale.

The paper also introduces U-Hop+, a sublinear-time algorithm for reaching the optimal capacity, and analyzes how the required feature dimension scales with the number of memories. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings. The geometric viewpoint links capacity, representation dimension, and memory arrangement, while the authors report benefits for retrieval in kernelized Hopfield models and representation learning in corresponding transformers.
neurips-2024-provably-optimal-memory-cap.tldr: A spherical-code connection yields tight asymptotic memory-capacity bounds and an algorithm for optimally configuring kernelized Hopfield memories.

paragraphs: Combining multiple face features can improve recognition when images are distant, low-resolution, or otherwise unconstrained. The difficulty is that some frames contain much more useful information than others. Existing fusion methods may require intermediate feature maps or face metadata that legacy databases storing only precomputed features cannot provide.

ProxyFusion uses proxy-based sparse expert selection and pooling to assign context-dependent importance within a feature set. Its computation grows linearly with the number of features, and changing their order does not change the result. The method works with stored features, generalizes to large sets, and uses substantially fewer parameters, supporting real-time and edge applications.

Qualitative experiments show that ProxyFusion learns information useful for weighting face features without accessing intermediate representations. Quantitative evaluations on IARPA BTS3.1 and DroneSURF report superior performance in challenging long-range, low-resolution verification settings. The contribution combines recognition effectiveness with a practical interface: feature aggregation can operate on representations that existing biometric template stores already contain.
neurips-2024-proxyfusion-face-feature-ag.tldr: ProxyFusion efficiently combines stored face features using sparse experts, improving recognition in evaluated long-range, low-resolution settings.

paragraphs: The privacy accounting for differentially private stochastic gradient descent depends on how training batches are sampled. This paper examines the common practice of implementing batches through shuffling while reporting privacy parameters calculated for Poisson subsampling. Its analysis shows substantial gaps between these sampling schemes in the mechanism used to analyze DP-SGD privacy.

The theoretical contribution gives new lower bounds for multi-epoch Adaptive Batch Linear Queries with shuffled batch sampling. Earlier analysis covered only one epoch. Extending the analysis to repeated passes makes the mismatch relevant to multi-epoch training and raises serious questions about applying Poisson-based accounting to a shuffled implementation.

The authors also introduce a practical way to perform Poisson subsampling at scale using massively parallel computation and use it to train models efficiently. They compare those models' utility with optimistic utility estimates for shuffling, informed by the new lower bounds. This connects the privacy-accounting issue to model usefulness while providing a scalable implementation of the sampling scheme assumed by Poisson-based analysis.
neurips-2024-scalable-dp-sgd-shuffling-v.tldr: Multi-epoch privacy bounds challenge using Poisson accounting for shuffled DP-SGD, while a parallel implementation makes Poisson sampling scalable.

paragraphs: Video-language continual learning asks models to keep learning from video and text while retaining earlier knowledge. ViLCo-Bench provides a dedicated benchmark for this relatively underexplored setting. It combines ten-minute videos with corresponding language queries drawn from publicly available datasets, supporting evaluation across a range of video-text tasks.

The benchmark brings together several challenges: long videos create memory demands, open language queries introduce linguistic complexity, and text may not align cleanly with video. The authors also propose a memory-efficient framework that uses self-supervised learning and mechanisms inspired by short-term and long-term memory effects to address these difficulties.

The intended contribution is to broaden continual learning evaluation beyond conventional tasks that add new classes over time. The authors argue that the benchmark's greater complexity can support research into video-language learning with difficult or limited annotations. The supplied abstract presents the benchmark and accompanying method as research infrastructure, with curated data and evaluations available to support further investigation of how models adapt without losing prior knowledge.
neurips-2024-vilco-bench-video-language-.tldr: ViLCo-Bench introduces long-video and language-query tasks for continual learning, alongside a memory-efficient learning framework.

paragraphs: Estimating a bird's-eye-view map from vehicle cameras requires coherent interpretation of the surrounding environment, including regions obscured or poorly captured in the images. VQ-Map addresses how image features can be connected to a generative model that supplies prior knowledge about plausible map layouts and their semantic elements.

The method learns a discrete representation of ground-truth maps using a generative model similar to a vector-quantized variational autoencoder. This produces map tokens and a codebook embedding that captures semantics of different map elements. A specialized token decoder aligns sparse image features with the learned map tokens, and the codebook bridges perspective-view information and bird's-eye-view map generation.

Evaluations report mean IoU values of 62.2 for surround-view and 47.6 for monocular estimation on nuScenes, plus 73.4 IoU for monocular estimation on Argoverse. The authors report these as new records for the task. The findings support using discrete map representations as the interface between incomplete visual evidence and a model of high-level map structure.
neurips-2024-vq-map-bird-s-eye-view-map-.tldr: VQ-Map aligns camera features with learned discrete map tokens to generate bird's-eye-view layouts with reported benchmark-record accuracy.

paragraphs: WorldCoder is a model-based language-model agent that represents its understanding of an environment as a Python program. It builds this program from interactions with the environment, turning experience into an explicit world model. The program is intended to explain what the agent has observed while supporting planning about achievable rewards.

The model must also remain optimistic about the rewards the agent can obtain. The paper formalizes this optimism as a logical constraint connecting the program and a planner. This makes the relationship between learned world knowledge and planning an explicit part of the approach. The code serves both as an explanation of experience and as a representation the agent can revise.

Experiments on gridworlds and task planning find greater sample efficiency than deep reinforcement learning and greater compute efficiency than ReAct-style agents. The authors also show knowledge transfer across environments through code editing. These findings support executable programs as reusable world models in the studied settings, with adaptation expressed through changes to the model's code.
neurips-2024-worldcoder-a-model-based-ll.tldr: WorldCoder learns editable Python world models from interaction, showing efficiency and transfer benefits in gridworlds and task planning.
